guitar.notes: Original entry already well-balanced; keeping as-is — Petty/Campbell's gear genuinely spans multiple iconic instruments without one being singularly dominant.

tone.target: bright clean jangle with slight compression
tone.profile: bright clean jangle with slight compression
tone.summary: The signal chain uses a light compressor for tight attack, followed by a bright pre-amp boost (OD 9) to enhance the jangle. The core sound is achieved using the Silver Twin amp model paired with the US 2x12 cab, adding subtle Chorus and Spring Reverb for the classic Telecaster chime.

rig.name: Tom Petty - Learning To Fly - Valeton GP-180

blocks.purpose: Clean up ambient noise and hum.
Provide tight clean attack and slight compression.
Add subtle grit and boost the high end for jangle.
blocks.gap: Using Blues OD instead of a dedicated bright booster to maintain clean character while adding definition.

blocks.purpose: Add the required subtle chorus effect for chime.

blocks.gap: The tone requires clean headroom, so no dedicated drive pedal is used.

blocks.purpose: Simulate the clean headroom and bright character of a Fender Twin.
Provide a bright, articulate sound suitable for single-coil guitars.
Fine-tune the frequency response to enhance chime and clarity.
Add the required classic spring reverb for vintage chime.
Add subtle depth without sounding like a 'bright delay' effect.
blocks.gap: The verdict suggested dropping bright delay, so settings are kept minimal and the module is used for texture rather than rhythm.

improvements.summary: Upgrade the cabinet IR for increased clarity and vintage chime.

proposals.reason: Enhance Telecaster chime and brightness beyond US 2x12.
